bib.title: Revisiting the Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
bib.venue: 35th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2021)

read.skipped: Appendix figure panels (Figs 15-20) are plot axis text only; read captions, not images.

question: Do recent state-of-the-art image classifiers still show the poor calibration reported for earlier networks, and how do accuracy, size, pretraining and architecture relate to it?
hypothesis: Implied: the reported trend that newer, more accurate models are worse calibrated may not extend to recent architectures.
contributions: Best current models (MLP-Mixer, ViT) are well calibrated and more robust to distribution shift
In-distribution calibration slightly deteriorates with model size, outweighed by accuracy gains
Under distribution shift calibration improves with model size
Accuracy and calibration correlate under distribution shift
Model size, pretraining duration and dataset size cannot fully explain calibration differences between families
Code and dataset of calibration measurements: 180 models, 16 families, 79 datasets, 28 metric variants

method.summary: Evaluates calibration (ECE, NLL, Brier) of publicly available pretrained image classifiers from 7 main families on ImageNet and OOD sets, unscaled and after temperature scaling fitted on 20% of ImageNet validation. Also trains BiT variants with controlled pretraining size and duration and EfficientNet-B4 with varying label smoothing.

datasets.name: ImageNet (ILSVRC-2012)
datasets.split: random 40,000 eval / 10,000 temperature fit of the public validation set

datasets.name: ImageNet-C
datasets.size: 15 perturbations x 5 severities = 75 datasets; 40,000 images each (excluding images used for temperature scaling)

datasets.name: ImageNet-21k
datasets.size: 14.2 million images, 21,000 classes (12.8M in main text)

other.note: appendix only; only family trained with label smoothing

inference.temperature: post-hoc temperature scaling: one logit scale fitted to maximise likelihood on the 20% held-out ImageNet validation images
inference.samples: one evaluation per model; seeds not stated

parameters.temperature_fit_set: 20% of ImageNet validation (10,000 images), randomly sampled

metrics.name: ECE (top-label)
metrics.definition: sum over bins |B_i|/n * |accuracy(B_i) - confidence(B_i)|, equal-mass binning, 100 bins

metrics.name: Selective-prediction cost
metrics.definition: linear combination of misclassification cost and abstention cost at a cost ratio and abstention rate

baselines: Guo et al. 2017 DenseNet-161 and ResNet-152 reported values
eval.protocol: Pareto comparison of ECE vs error per family; power-law fits with 95% bootstrap CIs; ECE variants (bins 15/100, equal-width/mass, L1/L2, top-label/all-label/class-wise) as robustness checks.

availability.weights: Model names link to used checkpoints where available (Table 1)

evidence.quote: we reserve 20% of the IMAGENET validation set (randomly sampled) for ﬁtting the temperature scaling parameter

results.claim: Recent families (MLP-Mixer, ViT, BiT) are both highly accurate and well calibrated; no general trend for recent or accurate networks to be poorly calibrated.
results.setup: ImageNet validation (40,000 eval images), pretrained then fine-tuned image classifiers, top-label ECE, 100 equal-mass bins, unscaled and temperature-scaled
results.quote: there is no general trend for recent or highly accurate neural networks to be poorly calibrated compared to older or less accurate models

results.setup: Released measurements; Table 1 lists only 28 model rows in 8 families and the main text 7 families
results.quote: comprising 180 distinct models from 16 families, each evaluated on 79 ImageNet-scale datasets and 28 metric variants

results.claim: After temperature scaling, ECE of BiT-R50x1 is unchanged across ImageNet, ImageNet-21k, JFT-300 pretraining.
results.setup: BiT-R50x1 pretrained on ImageNet (1.3M), ImageNet-21k (12.8M), JFT-300 (300M), fine-tuned on ImageNet, temperature-scaled

results.claim: Same for BiT-R101x3, ECE does not change consistently with pretraining data.
results.setup: BiT-R101x3, same three pretraining datasets, temperature-scaled

results.claim: Pretraining dataset size has no significant effect on calibration; longer pretraining only moves a model along its accuracy/calibration Pareto set.
results.setup: BiT R50x1 and R101x3, trained with matched schedules, steps held constant vs dataset size held constant
results.quote: pretraining dataset size has no signiﬁcant effect on calibration, while pre-training duration only shifts the model within its accuracy/calibration Pareto set

results.claim: Within most families larger models have higher in-distribution ECE but lower error, so each family sits on its own Pareto set.
results.setup: ImageNet validation (40,000 eval images), pretrained then fine-tuned image classifiers, top-label ECE, 100 equal-mass bins, temperature-scaled; ResNeXt-WSL is the exception
results.quote: larger members tend to have higher calibration error (Figure 2, right). However, at the same time, larger models have consistently lower classiﬁcation error

results.claim: Under distribution shift, calibration of larger models is more robust; size trend reverses for most families after temperature scaling.
results.setup: ImageNet-C, 5 severities, temperature fitted on clean ImageNet held-out 20%
results.quote: the trend is reversed for most model families as we move out of distribution, especially after accounting for conﬁdence bias by temperature scaling

results.claim: Calibration decay under ImageNet-C is slower for MLP-Mixer and ViT than other families.
results.quote: this decay in calibration performance is slower for MLP-Mixer and ViT than for the other model families, both before and after temperature scaling

results.claim: Models Pareto-optimal on ImageNet stay Pareto-optimal on natural OOD sets; accuracy and calibration strongly correlate OOD.
results.setup: ImageNetV2, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A (200-class logit subsets for R and A)
results.quote: models that are Pareto-optimal (i.e. no other model is both more accurate and better calibrated) on IMAGENET remain Pareto-optimal on the OOD datasets

results.claim: Selective prediction: the more accurate BiT-R152x4 (error better by 0.08) beats the better-ECE R50x1 (ECE better by 0.009) up to 70% abstention.
results.setup: BiT R152x4 vs R50x1, ImageNet and ImageNet-R, cost = linear combination of misclassification and abstention cost
results.quote: For abstention rates up to 70% (which covers most practical scenarios with abstention rates low enough for the model to be useful), the model with better accuracy has a lower overall cost than the model with better ECE

results.claim: ViT family pair: larger model has 0.076 lower error and 0.007 higher ECE, and still has lower decision cost.
results.setup: ViT B-32 vs H-14, selective prediction cost, all tested misclassification costs and abstention rates
results.note: Text says 0.194 vs 0.118 for the pair, in that order, as printed
results.quote: the bigger model has 0.076 lower classiﬁcation error (0.194 vs. 0.118) and 0.007 higher ECE (0.017 vs. 0.01)

results.claim: ViT-B/32 vs ResNeXt-WSL 32d: 0.03 error gap vs 0.03 ECE gap; better-accuracy model still preferred in most practical cost settings.
results.quote: The latter model has 0.03 lower (better) classiﬁcation error while the ViT model has 0.03 lower (better) ECE

results.claim: Longer-pretrained BiT-R101x3 has lower error (0.176 vs 0.232) but higher ECE (0.028 vs 0.019); lower error gives lower cost.
results.setup: BiT-R101x3 pretrained 113k vs 1120k steps, selective prediction
results.quote: for R101x3, 0.176 vs 0.232 in favor of the longer-trained model

results.claim: ECE vs classification error follows a power law y=a x^k; the ResNeXt WSL fit (a=0.19, k=1.03) is one the text calls a good fit.
results.setup: Fig 11 per-family fits of temperature-scaled ECE on error, 95% bootstrap CI; each dot a (model variant, dataset) pair; Fig 11 lists a and k per family
results.note: Panel a values read in layout order (MLP-Mixer 0.10, ViT 0.09, BiT 0.23, ResNeXt WSL 0.19 with k=1.03); the mapping to ResNeXt WSL is from Fig 11 panel order, not stated in running text.

results.claim: The sign of the ECE-vs-error relationship for temperature-scaled BiT models flips with the bin count (15, 100, 5000 bins).
results.setup: BiT ResNets varying size, pretraining dataset and duration, ImageNet, temperature-scaled; 15 bins (2667 pts/bin), 100 bins (400), 5000 bins (8)
results.quote: whether this relationship is positive or negative depends on the number of bins used for estimating ECE

results.claim: Binning bias of ECE (squared variant) falls with accuracy for models with at least 50% top-1 accuracy.
results.setup: Lemma 1, l2-ECE, assumes enough bins so delta<1/2
results.quote: Hence, for models that have at least 50% top-1 accuracy, increasing the accuracy reduces the bias.

results.claim: Label smoothing makes models artificially underconfident; without it plus temperature scaling gives the lowest ECE across ImageNet-C severities.
results.setup: EfficientNet-B4 trained with label smoothing 0, .03, .1, .3, .9 on ImageNet, evaluated on ImageNet-C
results.quote: training without label smoothing actually results in the lowest ECE across all IMAGENET-C severities

results.claim: Temperature scaling reveals trends hidden by over/underconfidence; ranks depend on ECE variant but Pareto-optimal families do not.
results.setup: Equal-width/mass, 15/100 bins, L1/L2, top-label, all-label, class-wise ECE variants
results.quote: the same model families tend to be Pareto-optimal across all ECE variants

limits: Image classification on ImageNet-scale data only; 2021 models.
Authors say ECE estimators are biased and rankings depend on ECE variant; they mitigate by Pareto reading with accuracy.
Architecture as determinant is a speculation (spatial inductive bias); further work needed to tell if it generalizes.
Pretraining ablations are on BiT only.
Cost analysis is one selective-prediction scenario; real cost structures may differ.
Training hyperparameters of the evaluated models and of the BiT pretraining runs and EfficientNet label smoothing runs are not given (refers to Kolesnikov et al. 2020).
ResNeXt-WSL is an exception to the size/calibration trade-off, not investigated.
